newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: YPF employees to appeal ban of share sale.
newsitem.headline: YPF employees to appeal ban of share sale.

text.p: The employees of oil firm who own 10 percent of its shares and the Argentine state will challenge a court ruling that banned their sale, the proxy for YPF's employees said Tuesday.
"The ruling is an aberration," Pablo Grigio Campana, proxy for YPF's 4,673 employees in the deal, told Reuters.
"It is a strange decision upholding a claim by 11 former YPF's employees who did not even have the right to participate in the program as they left the company before it was implemented."
Local press reports Tuesday said the claim was presented by some 1,000 former YPF's employees who argue they were left out of the operation.
Grigio Campana said nonetheless the deal would go ahead.
"Bids keep coming in," he said. "But potential buyers are warned about the judge's ruling."
He added Argentine government officials told him the state would also challenge the ruling.
The cut-off price for the auction of the YPF shares were set to be announced at 1015 local time/1315 GMT Tuesday, an executive for a local bank handling the auction said Monday.

Banco Comafi and Merchant Bankers Asociados, an Argentine affiliate of Salomon Brothers Inc as well as Salomon Brothers in New York, have been accepting bids for the shares since 1700 local time Monday.
Argentina's government authorized the sale of the 33.5 million Class C YPF shares in the hands of the company's employees --10 percent of the firm's stock -- by a decree issued last Friday.
The government owns another 20 percent of the firm but says it has no immediate plans to sell.
